title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only work at the document level (or on narrow, task-specific token tasks such as spell checking), so they cannot localize which tokens in a text are anomalous. The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, releases three token-annotated benchmarks (SMS_Spam with injected character corruption, Restaurant Review semantic anomalies, Grammar errors), and proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal word-level token embeddings (BERT-base-uncased embeddings aggregated by element-wise max pooling over subwords) and scores each test token by its nearest-neighbor distance, aggregating token scores by mean for document-level scores. TokenCore achieves the best average token-level AUROC (0.7145) and document-level AUROC (0.7335) among 7 methods, ranking first at token level on Review (0.8271) and Grammar (0.6371) and at document level on Review (0.9594), while ECOD/iForest remain better on the character-corruption SMS_Spam token-level task.

requirements.stmt: Word-level token embeddings must be formed by element-wise max pooling over the embeddings of all subwords of that word (Equation 1), not by taking the first subword or averaging.
requirements.cite: Section 5, Embedding Extraction with Max Pooling, Eq. (1)
requirements.quote: To maximize the anomaly signal for each token, we propose using max pooling to aggregate subword embeddings.

requirements.stmt: A memory bank must be built from the word-level embeddings of all tokens in the normal training documents only (no anomalous-token embeddings are stored).
requirements.quote: we extract word-level embeddings from all normal samples in the training set and store them in a memory bank

requirements.stmt: The token-level anomaly score is the minimum distance from the test-token embedding to any memory-bank entry (Equation 2); larger distance means more anomalous.

requirements.stmt: Document-level anomaly scores must be obtained by mean aggregation of the token-level scores over all tokens of the document (Equation 3).

why: The authors released the method code (TokenCore.py: memory bank + nearest-neighbor token scoring), the alignment/annotation utilities (align.py, tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py) and all three annotated datasets locally in data/ (grammar .npy/.json, restaurant_review, sms_spam), so the core logic can be kept verbatim. What is NOT released is a runnable entrypoint: the only end-to-end artifact is Demo.ipynb (with frozen outputs), there is no requirements.txt, and TokenCore.py consumes precomputed token-embedding matrices, so the BERT-base-uncased embedding extraction, the 50/50 split and the token-level AUROC computation have to be rebuilt as a script from the notebook before the target number for Grammar (C1) can be produced. Keep authors' logic, rebuild the missing driver.
est_runtime: ~25-35 min wall clock on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM: ~10 min installing torch (CPU wheel), transformers, scikit-learn; ~1 min BERT-base download; ~1-3 min BERT forward pass over 300 short Grammar documents; seconds for the max-pooling, memory-bank build and brute-force nearest-neighbor scoring; plus the driver-script rewrite from the notebook and one clean end-to-end re-run.
blockers: no dependency file: torch/transformers/sklearn/numpy must be pinned by hand (works on Python 3.12)
TokenCore.py takes embedding matrices only; the BERT max-pooling-over-subwords front-end exists only inside the notebook, so the pipeline must be extracted into a script
Demo.ipynb is 3.8 MB of stored outputs; it must be rewritten/cleared before execution
no GPU on this machine (BERT-base CPU inference only, which is acceptable at this scale)

Grammar token-level AUROC is computed over very few anomalous tokens (~15 anomalous docs in the test half), and the split is random, so the absolute value 0.6371 will depend on the split seed and may drift

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction of claim C1: TokenCore's token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (0.6371, tolerance ±0.02 absolute). We clone the authors' repo, keep TokenCore.py/align.py/json_to_npy.py verbatim, and rebuild only the missing driver that Demo.ipynb used to hide: read the released grammar annotations (data/grammar_correction_labeled.json and data/grammar.npy), build the 300-document corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10), take 50% of the normal documents as the memory-bank training set (R6, A8), run BERT-base-uncased over the remaining normal + anomalous documents, max-pool subword embeddings into word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1, R2/R9, A3/A4), fit the authors' TextCore memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3, A2), score every test token by Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4, A1/A9), and compute pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC plus the mean-aggregated document-level scores (Eq. 3, R5, A5). The paper value is a single split-free number, so the only real drift risk is split randomness on 300 short documents; we therefore report a primary seeded run plus a small multi-seed spread so the ±0.02 band can be interpreted. Only the Grammar dataset is needed for C1, but the same driver is written so that running it on restaurant_review / sms_spam later costs nothing extra.
steps: Clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git into ./TokenCore and record the commit hash; do not modify TokenCore.py, align.py or tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py.

Create a venv/conda env on Python 3.12 and pip install torch (CPU wheel from the default index), transformers, numpy, scikit-learn, tqdm, requests; write the resolved versions into requirements.txt (the file the README references but the repo lacks).

Run src/inspect_data.py: dump shapes/dtypes/keys of data/grammar.npy and the JSON schema of data/grammar_correction_labeled.json, and print the actual class/function signatures of TokenCore.py and align.py. Decide the exact field names for words, token labels and document labels, and confirm the .npy is a token/label array rather than precomputed embeddings (43 KB is far too small for 300x768 floats).

Implement src/data_grammar.py against the inspected schema; load all 300 Grammar documents and hard-assert 300 documents / 270 normal / 30 anomalous (10% rate, R10) and consistency of the document labels with the token labels (R11).

Implement the split: with seed 0, shuffle the 270 normal documents, take the first 135 as the memory-bank training set; the test set is the other 135 normal documents plus all 30 anomalous documents (165 docs). Export the token-level gold labels for every test token.

Implement src/embed_bert.py: tokenize with BertTokenizerFast(return_offsets_mapping / word_ids), run BertModel in eval() with torch.no_grad() in batches of 32, max_length 128, take last_hidden_state, drop special tokens, and element-wise max-pool subwords per word unit. Assert a 1:1 map between produced word units and the gold word tokens in the annotated JSON; if align.py exposes an alignment helper, call it instead of re-implementing.

Implement src/detector.py: import the authors' TokenCore (use the real class name found by inspect_data.py, README shows both TokenCore and TextCore) and its fit / decision_function, fit on the normal-training token embedding matrix (no anomalous tokens, R3) and score the test token embeddings (R4).

Implement src/evaluate.py: token-level AUROC/AUPRC pooled over all test tokens (micro), document-level scores as the per-document mean of token scores (R5) and their AUROC/AUPRC, plus a random-score control (expected AUROC ~0.5) to validate the metric plumbing.
Wire reproduce.py to run the whole chain end-to-end; run the smoke configuration first (see smoke_test) and confirm all assertions on counts and shapes pass.
Run the intermediate checks (see intermediate_checks) before the full run.

Full run: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --seed 0 (CPU-only BERT inference over 300 short sentences, seconds for the memory bank and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour search). Write results/metrics.json.

If |token_auroc_grammar - 0.6371| > 0.02, re-run with seeds 1 and 2 and inspect sensitivity: report the per-seed values and mean/std, and check the highest-risk choices first (A5 micro vs per-document AUROC, A1/A9 Euclidean on unnormalized embeddings, A4 whether punctuation units are scored).
Write the final results/metrics.json containing the primary value, the multi-seed spread, the target, the tolerance band and an explicit pass/fail flag.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --smoke --seed 0 -> loads the released grammar annotations, keeps only the first 8 normal + first 2 anomalous documents (forcing the split so both sides are non-empty), runs one BERT-base forward pass over those 10 documents, max-pools subwords, builds a ~100-200 entry memory bank, scores the test tokens, and prints token_auroc/token_auprc plus every shape (n_docs, n_word_units, n_bank_tokens, n_test_tokens, n_positive_tokens). Success = no exception, finite scores, 1:1 alignment between word units and gold tokens, and AUROC in [0,1]. This exercises every stage of the data flow in under a minute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset size and label rate: exactly 300 documents, 270 normal (token_labels all 0) and 30 anomalous (>=1 token_label = 1) = 10% anomaly rate (R10); stop if the released file deviates.
Document/token label consistency: every document with at least one 1 token has doc_label 1 and vice versa (R11).

Token-level class balance: report total tokens, total anomalous tokens and their fraction across all 300 docs, and across the 165 test docs; sanity expectation is a few percent (the contract quotes token AUPRC ~0.04 for Grammar, which is roughly the positive rate) and only a handful of positives, so AUROC variance across seeds will be large - this justifies the ±0.02 band.
Alignment coverage: fraction of gold word tokens that receive a BERT word unit (target 1.0); log any word that tokenizes to zero subwords or overflows max_length=128.
Split sizes: 135 normal training docs and 135 normal + 30 anomalous test docs with seed 0; training set contains zero anomalous tokens (R3).

Memory bank size: n_bank_tokens should equal the total number of word units in the 135 normal training documents (report it; expect a few thousand) - a much smaller number means documents were dropped silently.

Parameter/embedding check: assert the token embedding width is 768 and that the pooling really is element-wise max (a max-pooled vector must equal the coordinate-wise max of its subword vectors on a hand-checked example).

Sanity baseline: random token scores give AUROC ~0.5 and AUPRC ~positive rate; TokenCore scores on the training tokens themselves (excluding self-matches) give near-zero distances, confirming the nearest-neighbour direction (higher distance = more anomalous, R4).
Metric parity: verify the AUROC/AUPRC implementation against sklearn.roc_auc_score / average_precision_score on synthetic labels, so the 0.6371 comparison cannot fail for plumbing reasons.
budget_plan: Total ~30-35 min on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM. Setup 10 min: clone the repo (<1 min) and pip install the CPU torch wheel plus transformers/scikit-learn (~8-9 min, ~5 GB, the dominant cost). Reconnaissance 3 min: inspect_data.py plus reading TokenCore.py/align.py and the JSON schema. Implementation 8 min: data_grammar.py, embed_bert.py, detector.py, evaluate.py, reproduce.py, requirements.txt. Smoke 2 min: 10-document subset end-to-end. Intermediate checks 2 min: counts, rates, alignment coverage, bank size, metric parity. Full run 3-4 min: one BERT-base forward pass over 300 short Grammar sentences on CPU (1-3 min) plus seconds of max-pooling and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour scoring. Verification 3 min: compare against 0.6371 with the ±0.02 band, and if out of band spend up to 5 more minutes on seeds 1 and 2 and on the highest-risk assumptions (A5, A1/A9, A4). Keep ~3 min slack; only the Grammar dataset is run, so no SMS_Spam/Review time is spent.

   19|         self.aggregation = aggregation
   20|         self.nbrs = None

   22|     def fit(self, X):

   24|         Fit the model using X as training data
   25|         
   26|         Parameters

   29|             Training data
   30|             
   31|         Returns

   33|         self : object
   34|             Fitted estimator
   35|         """
   36|         self.nbrs = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=self.n_neighbors).fit(X)

    1| # TokenCore
    2| 
    3| Official code and datasets for the paper
    4| **[Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection](https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.13644)** (WWW '26).
    5| 
    6| TokenCore is a memory-bank method for **token-level text anomaly detection**: instead of only flagging whole documents as anomalous, it localizes *which specific tokens* are anomalous. It builds a memory bank of normal token embeddings and scores each test token by its distance to the nearest normal neighbor, then aggregates token scores to obtain document-level scores.
    7| 
    8| ## Datasets
    9| 
   10| The three benchmark datasets are hosted on the Hugging Face Hub:
   11| 
   12| 👉 **[https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD)**
   13| 
   14| Each dataset provides both document-level and token-level anomaly annotations.
   15| 
   16| | Dataset | Anomaly type | Documents | Anomalies | Rate |
   17| |---|---|---|---|---|
   18| | SMS Spam | Character-level (corrupted sequences) | 4,518 | 393 | 8.7% |
   19| | Restaurant Review | Semantic (negative sentiment) | 1,100 | 50 | 4.5% |
   20| | Grammar Correction | Grammatical errors | 300 | 30 | 10% |
   21| 
   22| A local copy is also available in the `data/` folder.
   23| 
   24| ## Installation
   25| 
   26| ```bash
   27| git clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git
   28| cd TokenCore
   29| pip install -r requirements.txt
   30| ```
   31| 
   32| ## Quick Start
   33| 
   34| ```python
   35| from TokenCore import TextCore
   36| 
   37| model = TokenCore()
   38| 
   39| # Fit on normal token embeddings
   40| model.fit(X_train)
   41| 
   42| # Get token-level anomaly scores
   43| scores = model.decision_function(X_test)
   44| ```
   45| 
   46| `X_train` and `X_test` are token embedding matrices (e.g. BERT embeddings with max-pooling over subwords). See `Demo.ipynb` for the full pipeline, including embedding extraction, token-level scoring, and document-level aggregation.
   47| 
   48| ## Repository Structure
   49| 
   50| ```
   51| TokenCore/
   52| ├── data/           # Benchmark datasets (also on Hugging Face Hub)
   53| ├── TokenCore.py     # TokenCore method implementation

import json
import numpy as np

# Load JSON
with open('repo/data/grammar_correction_labeled.json', 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Load NPY
arr = np.load('repo/data/grammar.npy', allow_pickle=True)
inner = arr.item()
sentences = inner['sentences']
tokens = inner['tokens']
labels = inner['labels']

print('Sentences:', len(sentences))
print('Tokens lists:', len(tokens))
print('Labels lists:', len(labels))

# Check consistency with JSON doc labels
json_labels = [d['data']['label'] for d in data]
npy_doc_labels = [1 if any(l == 1 for l in lab) else 0 for lab in labels]

print('\nJSON doc labels - 0:', json_labels.count(0), '1:', json_labels.count(1))
print('NPY doc labels - 0:', npy_doc_labels.count(0), '1:', npy_doc_labels.count(1))

mismatch = sum(1 for a, b in zip(json_labels, npy_doc_labels) if a != b)
print('Mismatches:', mismatch)

# Show some anomalous docs
print('\nAnomalous docs (token labels = 1):')
for i, lab in enumerate(labels):
    if any(l == 1 for l in lab):
        print(f'  Doc {i}: tokens={tokens[i]}, labels={lab}')
        if i > 5:
            break

# Show token counts

total_anomalous = sum(sum(lab) for lab in labels)
print(f'\nTotal tokens: {total_tokens}')
print(f'Total anomalous tokens: {total_anomalous}')
print(f'Anomalous token rate: {total_anomalous/total_tokens:.4f}')

# Check token-level labels in JSON annotations
print('\nJSON annotation details for first anomalous doc:')
for i, d in enumerate(data):

"""
Load Grammar Correction dataset and create train/test split.
50% of normal documents for training, rest (normal + anomalous) for testing.
"""
import json
import numpy as np
from typing import List, Dict, Tuple


def load_grammar(data_dir: str = "repo/data") -> List[Dict]:
    """Load grammar dataset from .npy and JSON files."""
    # Load token-level annotations from .npy
    npy_path = f"{data_dir}/grammar.npy"
    arr = np.load(npy_path, allow_pickle=True)
    inner = arr.item()
    sentences = inner['sentences']
    tokens = inner['tokens']
    labels = inner['labels']

    # Load document-level labels from JSON
    json_path = f"{data_dir}/grammar_correction_labeled.json"
    with open(json_path, 'r') as f:
        json_data = json.load(f)
    json_labels = [d['data']['label'] for d in json_data]

    # Build documents
    documents = []
    for i in range(len(sentences)):
        doc = {
            'id': i,
            'text': sentences[i][0] if isinstance(sentences[i], list) else sentences[i],
            'tokens': tokens[i],
            'token_labels': labels[i],
            'doc_label': json_labels[i],
        }
        documents.append(doc)

    return documents


def verify_dataset(documents: List[Dict]) -> None:
    """Verify dataset properties match paper claims."""
    n_docs = len(documents)
    n_normal = sum(1 for d in documents if d['doc_label'] == 0)
    n_anomalous = sum(1 for d in documents if d['doc_label'] == 1)

    assert n_docs == 300, f"Expected 300 docs, got {n_docs}"
    assert n_normal == 270, f"Expected 270 normal docs, got {n_normal}"
    assert n_anomalous == 30, f"Expected 30 anomalous docs, got {n_anomalous}"

    # Verify doc_label consistency with token_labels
    for d in documents:
        has_anomalous_token = any(l == 1 for l in d['token_labels'])
        assert d['doc_label'] == (1 if has_anomalous_token else 0), \
            f"Doc {d['id']}: doc_label={d['doc_label']} but token_labels={d['token_labels']}"

    total_tokens = sum(len(d['tokens']) for d in documents)
    total_anomalous = sum(sum(d['token_labels']) for d in documents)
    print(f"Dataset verified: {n_docs} docs ({n_normal} normal, {n_anomalous} anomalous)")
    print(f"Total tokens: {total_tokens}, anomalous tokens: {total_anomalous} ({total_anomalous/total_tokens:.4f})")


def split_documents(documents: List[Dict], seed: int = 0) -> Tuple[List[Dict], List[Dict]]:
    """
    Split: 50% of normal documents for training, rest for testing.
    Test set includes remaining normal + all anomalous documents.
    """
    normal_docs = [d for d in documents if d['doc_label'] == 0]
    anomalous_docs = [d for d in documents if d['doc_label'] == 1]

    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    rng.shuffle(normal_docs)

    n_train = len(normal_docs) // 2
    train_docs = normal_docs[:n_train]
    test_docs = normal_docs[n_train:] + anomalous_docs

    return train_docs, test_docs


if __name__ == "__main__":
    docs = load_grammar()
    verify_dataset(docs)
    train, test = split_documents(docs, seed=0)
    print(f"Train: {len(train)} docs, Test: {len(test)} docs")
    train_tokens = sum(len(d['tokens']) for d in train)
    test_tokens = sum(len(d['tokens']) for d in test)
    print(f"Train tokens: {train_tokens}, Test tokens: {test_tokens}")

"""
Extract BERT-base-uncased word-level embeddings with max-pooling over subwords.
"""
import torch
import numpy as np
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel
from typing import List, Dict, Tuple
from tqdm import tqdm


def get_tokenizer_model(model_name: str = "bert-base-uncased", device: str = None):
    """Load tokenizer and model."""
    if device is None:
        device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = model.to(device).eval()
    return tokenizer, model, device


def embed_documents(
    documents: List[Dict],
    tokenizer,
    model,
    device: str,
    max_length: int = 128,
    batch_size: int = 32,
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """
    Extract word-level embeddings for all documents.
    Returns:
        embeddings: (n_tokens, 768) array of all word-level embeddings
        token_labels: (n_tokens,) array of corresponding token labels
        doc_ids: (n_tokens,) array of document ids for each token
    """
    all_embeddings = []
    all_labels = []
    all_doc_ids = []

    # Process in batches for efficiency
    # For simplicity, process one doc at a time since we need word alignment
    for doc in tqdm(documents, desc="Embedding documents"):
        tokens = doc['tokens']
        token_labels = doc['token_labels']
        doc_id = doc['id']

        # Tokenize
        encoded = tokenizer(
            tokens,
            is_split_into_words=True,
            return_tensors="pt",
            truncation=True,
            max_length=max_length,
            padding=False,
        )

        input_ids = encoded["input_ids"].to(device)
        attention_mask = encoded["attention_mask"].to(device)

        with torch.no_grad():
            outputs = model(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask)
            last_hidden_state = outputs.last_hidden_state[0].cpu().numpy()  # (seq_len, 768)

        word_ids = encoded.word_ids(batch_index=0)

        # Max-pool subwords to word level
        word_embeddings = []
        word_labels = []
        current_word_idx = None
        current_subwords = []

        for pos, word_idx in enumerate(word_ids):
            if word_idx is None:
                continue  # Skip [CLS], [SEP], [PAD]

            if word_idx != current_word_idx:
                # New word - finalize previous
                if current_subwords:
                    pooled = np.max(np.stack(current_subwords), axis=0)
                    word_embeddings.append(pooled)
                    word_labels.append(token_labels[current_word_idx])

                current_word_idx = word_idx
                current_subwords = [last_hidden_state[pos]]
            else:
                current_subwords.append(last_hidden_state[pos])

        # Finalize last word
        if current_subwords and current_word_idx is not None:
            pooled = np.max(np.stack(current_subwords), axis=0)
            word_embeddings.append(pooled)
            word_labels.append(token_labels[current_word_idx])

        # Verify alignment
        assert len(word_embeddings) == len(tokens), \
            f"Doc {doc_id}: got {len(word_embeddings)} word embeddings but {len(tokens)} tokens"

        all_embeddings.extend(word_embeddings)
        all_labels.extend(word_labels)
        all_doc_ids.extend([doc_id] * len(word_embeddings))

    return (
        np.array(all_embeddings, dtype=np.float32),
        np.array(all_labels, dtype=np.int64),
        np.array(all_doc_ids, dtype=np.int64),
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from data_grammar import load_grammar, split_documents
    docs = load_grammar()
    train, test = split_documents(docs, seed=0)
    tokenizer, model, device = get_tokenizer_model()
    print(f"Device: {device}")

    # Test on small subset
    X_test, y_test, doc_ids = embed_documents(test[:5], tokenizer, model, device)
    print(f"Test embeddings shape: {X_test.shape}")
    print(f"Test labels shape: {y_test.shape}")
    print(f"Positive tokens: {y_test.sum()}")

"""
Adapter for TokenCore memory-bank detector.
"""
import numpy as np
import sys
import os

# Add repo to path so we can import TokenCore
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', 'repo'))
from TokenCore import TokenCore


def create_detector() -> TokenCore:
    """Create TokenCore detector with default settings (n_neighbors=1)."""
    return TokenCore(n_neighbors=1, aggregation='mean')


def fit_detector(detector: TokenCore, X_train: np.ndarray) -> TokenCore:
    """Fit detector on normal training token embeddings."""
    detector.fit(X_train)
    return detector


def score_tokens(detector: TokenCore, X_test: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Score test tokens. Higher distance = more anomalous."""
    return detector.decision_function(X_test)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Quick sanity check
    X_train = np.random.randn(100, 768).astype(np.float32)
    X_test = np.random.randn(20, 768).astype(np.float32)
    detector = create_detector()
    fit_detector(detector, X_train)
    scores = score_tokens(detector, X_test)
    print(f"Scores shape: {scores.shape}, min: {scores.min():.4f}, max: {scores.max():.4f}")

"""
Compute AUROC and AUPRC metrics.
"""
import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score
from typing import Dict, Tuple


def compute_metrics(y_true: np.ndarray, y_scores: np.ndarray) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """
    Compute token-level AUROC and AUPRC.
    y_true: binary labels (0/1)
    y_scores: anomaly scores (higher = more anomalous)
    """
    # Handle edge cases
    if len(np.unique(y_true)) < 2:
        # Only one class present
        auroc = 0.5
        auprc = y_true.mean()
    else:
        auroc = roc_auc_score(y_true, y_scores)
        auprc = average_precision_score(y_true, y_scores)

    return {
        'auroc': float(auroc),
        'auprc': float(auprc),
        'n_samples': int(len(y_true)),
        'n_positive': int(y_true.sum()),
        'positive_rate': float(y_true.mean()),
    }


def compute_document_scores(
    token_scores: np.ndarray,
    doc_ids: np.ndarray,
    doc_labels: Dict[int, int],
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """
    Aggregate token scores to document level by mean.
    Returns:
        doc_scores: (n_docs,) mean token score per document
        doc_true: (n_docs,) document labels
    """
    unique_docs = np.unique(doc_ids)
    doc_scores = []
    doc_true = []

    for doc_id in unique_docs:
        mask = doc_ids == doc_id
        doc_score = token_scores[mask].mean()
        doc_scores.append(doc_score)
        doc_true.append(doc_labels[int(doc_id)])

    return np.array(doc_scores), np.array(doc_true)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Test with synthetic data
    y_true = np.array([0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1])
    y_scores = np.array([0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.8, 0.7, 0.9])
    metrics = compute_metrics(y_true, y_scores)
    print("Test metrics:", metrics)

import os
import sys
import time
import numpy as np
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

# Add src to path
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'src'))

from embed_bert import get_tokenizer_model, embed_documents

def run_single_seed(
    documents: List[Dict],
    seed: int,
    model_name: str = "bert-base-uncased",
    max_length: int = 128,
    device: str = None,
) -> Dict:
    """Run full pipeline for a single seed."""
    if device is None:
        device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

    # Split
    train_docs, test_docs = split_documents(documents, seed=seed)

    # Load model
    tokenizer, model, device = get_tokenizer_model(model_name, device)

    # Extract embeddings
    print(f"Extracting embeddings for {len(train_docs)} train + {len(test_docs)} test docs...")
    X_train, y_train, doc_ids_train = embed_documents(train_docs, tokenizer, model, device, max_length)
    X_test, y_test, doc_ids_test = embed_documents(test_docs, tokenizer, model, device, max_length)

    print(f"Train: {X_train.shape[0]} tokens, Test: {X_test.shape[0]} tokens")
    print(f"Test positive tokens: {y_test.sum()} / {len(y_test)} ({y_test.mean():.4f})")

    # Fit detector
    detector = create_detector()
    fit_detector(detector, X_train)

    # Score test tokens
    token_scores = score_tokens(detector, X_test)

    # Token-level metrics
    token_metrics = compute_metrics(y_test, token_scores)

    # Document-level metrics
    doc_labels = {d['id']: d['doc_label'] for d in documents}
    doc_scores, doc_true = compute_document_scores(token_scores, doc_ids_test, doc_labels)
    doc_metrics = compute_metrics(doc_true, doc_scores)

    # Sanity: training tokens should have low scores (near neighbors)
    train_scores = score_tokens(detector, X_train)
    print(f"Train token scores - mean: {train_scores.mean():.4f}, std: {train_scores.std():.4f}")
    print(f"Test token scores - mean: {token_scores.mean():.4f}, std: {token_scores.std():.4f}")

    return {

        'token_auroc': token_metrics['auroc'],
        'token_auprc': token_metrics['auprc'],

        'n_bank_tokens': int(X_train.shape[0]),
        'n_test_tokens': int(X_test.shape[0]),
        'n_positive_tokens': int(y_test.sum()),
        'token_positive_rate': float(y_test.mean()),
        'train_token_score_mean': float(train_scores.mean()),
        'test_token_score_mean': float(token_scores.mean()),
    }

"""
Reproduce TokenCore token-level AUROC on Grammar dataset (Claim C1).
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time
import numpy as np
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

# Add src to path
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'src'))

from data_grammar import load_grammar, verify_dataset, split_documents
from embed_bert import get_tokenizer_model, embed_documents
from detector import create_detector, fit_detector, score_tokens
from evaluate import compute_metrics, compute_document_scores


def run_single_seed(
    documents: List[Dict],
    seed: int,
    model_name: str = "bert-base-uncased",
    max_length: int = 128,
    device: str = None,
) -> Dict:
    """Run full pipeline for a single seed."""
    if device is None:
        device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

    # Split
    train_docs, test_docs = split_documents(documents, seed=seed)

    # Load model
    tokenizer, model, device = get_tokenizer_model(model_name, device)

    # Extract embeddings
    print(f"Extracting embeddings for {len(train_docs)} train + {len(test_docs)} test docs...")
    X_train, y_train, doc_ids_train = embed_documents(train_docs, tokenizer, model, device, max_length)
    X_test, y_test, doc_ids_test = embed_documents(test_docs, tokenizer, model, device, max_length)

    print(f"Train: {X_train.shape[0]} tokens, Test: {X_test.shape[0]} tokens")
    print(f"Test positive tokens: {y_test.sum()} / {len(y_test)} ({y_test.mean():.4f})")

    # Fit detector
    detector = create_detector()
    fit_detector(detector, X_train)

    # Score test tokens
    token_scores = score_tokens(detector, X_test)

    # Token-level metrics
    token_metrics = compute_metrics(y_test, token_scores)

    # Document-level metrics
    doc_labels = {d['id']: d['doc_label'] for d in documents}
    doc_scores, doc_true = compute_document_scores(token_scores, doc_ids_test, doc_labels)
    doc_metrics = compute_metrics(doc_true, doc_scores)

    # Sanity: training tokens should have low scores (near neighbors)
    train_scores = score_tokens(detector, X_train)
    print(f"Train token scores - mean: {train_scores.mean():.4f}, std: {train_scores.std():.4f}")
    print(f"Test token scores - mean: {token_scores.mean():.4f}, std: {token_scores.std():.4f}")

    return {
        'seed': seed,
        'token_auroc': token_metrics['auroc'],
        'token_auprc': token_metrics['auprc'],
        'doc_auroc': doc_metrics['auroc'],
        'doc_auprc': doc_metrics['auprc'],
        'n_train_docs': len(train_docs),
        'n_test_docs': len(test_docs),
        'n_bank_tokens': int(X_train.shape[0]),
        'n_test_tokens': int(X_test.shape[0]),
        'n_positive_tokens': int(y_test.sum()),
        'token_positive_rate': float(y_test.mean()),
        'train_token_score_mean': float(train_scores.mean()),
        'test_token_score_mean': float(token_scores.mean()),
    }


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Reproduce TokenCore Grammar results")
    parser.add_argument('--datasets', default='grammar', help='Dataset to run')
    parser.add_argument('--seed', type=int, default=None, help='Random seed (overrides --seeds)')
    parser.add_argument('--smoke', action='store_true', help='Run smoke test with tiny subset')
    parser.add_argument('--seeds', type=str, default='0', help='Comma-separated seeds to run')
    parser.add_argument('--max-length', type=int, default=128, help='Max sequence length')
    args = parser.parse_args()

    # --seed overrides --seeds
    if args.seed is not None:
        seeds = [args.seed]
    else:
        seeds = [int(s.strip()) for s in args.seeds.split(',')]

    if args.datasets != 'grammar':
        print(f"Dataset {args.datasets} not implemented yet")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Load data
    print("Loading Grammar dataset...")
    documents = load_grammar()
    verify_dataset(documents)

    if args.smoke:
        print("Running smoke test with 10 documents...")
        # Take 8 normal + 2 anomalous
        normal = [d for d in documents if d['doc_label'] == 0][:8]
        anomalous = [d for d in documents if d['doc_label'] == 1][:2]
        documents = normal + anomalous
        print(f"Smoke subset: {len(documents)} docs")

    # Run seeds
    results = []

    for seed in seeds:
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print(f"Running seed {seed}")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        start = time.time()
        result = run_single_seed(
            documents,
            seed=seed,
            max_length=args.max_length,
        )
        result['runtime_seconds'] = time.time() - start
        results.append(result)
        print(f"Seed {seed} completed in {result['runtime_seconds']:.1f}s")
        print(f"  Token AUROC: {result['token_auroc']:.4f}")
        print(f"  Token AUPRC: {result['token_auprc']:.4f}")
        print(f"  Doc AUROC:   {result['doc_auroc']:.4f}")

    # Aggregate results
    primary = results[0]
    if len(results) > 1:
        token_aurocs = [r['token_auroc'] for r in results]
        token_auprcs = [r['token_auprc'] for r in results]
        primary['token_auroc_mean'] = float(np.mean(token_aurocs))
        primary['token_auroc_std'] = float(np.std(token_aurocs))
        primary['token_auprc_mean'] = float(np.mean(token_auprcs))
        primary['token_auprc_std'] = float(np.std(token_auprcs))
        primary['all_seeds'] = results

    # Write results

"""
Extract BERT word-level embeddings using the repo's align.py extract_word_embeddings.
"""
import sys
import os
import numpy as np
from typing import List, Dict, Tuple

# Import the repo's alignment function
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', 'repo'))
from align import extract_word_embeddings
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel
import torch


def get_tokenizer_model(model_name: str = "bert-base-cased", device: str = None):
    """Load tokenizer and model."""
    if device is None:
        device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = model.to(device).eval()
    return tokenizer, model, device


def embed_documents(
    documents: List[Dict],
    tokenizer,
    model,
    device: str,
    model_name: str = "bert-base-cased",
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """
    Extract word-level embeddings for all documents using the repo's extract_word_embeddings.
    Returns:
        embeddings: (n_tokens, 768) array of all word-level embeddings
        token_labels: (n_tokens,) array of corresponding token labels
        doc_ids: (n_tokens,) array of document ids for each token
    """
    # Prepare inputs for extract_word_embeddings
    all_tokens = [d['tokens'] for d in documents]
    all_labels = [d['token_labels'] for d in documents]
    doc_ids = [d['id'] for d in documents]

    # Run the repo's alignment function
    with torch.no_grad():
        result = extract_word_embeddings(
            model=model,
            tokenizer=tokenizer,
            all_tokens=all_tokens,
            all_labels=all_labels,
            model_name=model_name,
            device=device
        )

    # Flatten results
    all_embeddings = []
    all_token_labels = []
    all_doc_ids = []

    for doc_idx, doc_data in enumerate(result):
        for item in doc_data:
            all_embeddings.append(item['embedding'])
            all_token_labels.append(item['label'])
            all_doc_ids.append(doc_ids[doc_idx])

    embeddings = np.array(all_embeddings, dtype=np.float32)
    token_labels = np.array(all_token_labels, dtype=np.int64)
    doc_ids_arr = np.array(all_doc_ids, dtype=np.int64)

    return embeddings, token_labels, doc_ids_arr


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Quick test
    from data_grammar import load_grammar, split_documents
    docs = load_grammar()
    train, test = split_documents(docs, seed=0)
    tokenizer, model, device = get_tokenizer_model()
    print('Device:', device)
    X_test, y_test, doc_ids = embed_documents(test[:5], tokenizer, model, device)
    print('Test embeddings shape:', X_test.shape)
    print('Test labels shape:', y_test.shape)
    print('Positive tokens:', y_test.sum())
    print('Doc IDs:', doc_ids)

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, 'repo')
from align import extract_word_embeddings
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel
import torch
import numpy as np

# Load all grammar docs
arr = np.load('repo/data/grammar.npy', allow_pickle=True)
inner = arr.item()
tokens = inner['tokens']
labels = inner['labels']

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('bert-base-cased')
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained('bert-base-cased')
model.eval()

with torch.no_grad():
    result = extract_word_embeddings(
        model=model,
        tokenizer=tokenizer,
        all_tokens=tokens,
        all_labels=labels,
        model_name='bert-base-cased',
        device='cpu'
    )

# Verify alignment for all docs
all_match = True
mismatches = []
for i, (doc_data, gold_tokens, gold_labels) in enumerate(zip(result, tokens, labels)):
    produced_tokens = [item['token'] for item in doc_data]
    produced_labels = [item['label'] for item in doc_data]
    
    if len(gold_tokens) != len(produced_tokens):
        all_match = False
        mismatches.append((i, len(gold_tokens), len(produced_tokens)))
    elif gold_tokens != produced_tokens:
        all_match = False
        mismatches.append((i, gold_tokens, produced_tokens))
    elif gold_labels != produced_labels:
        all_match = False
        mismatches.append((i, gold_labels, produced_labels))

print(f"Total docs: {len(tokens)}")
print(f"All alignments match: {all_match}")
if mismatches:
    print(f"Mismatches ({len(mismatches)}):")
    for m in mismatches[:5]:
        print(f"  {m}")
else:
    print("No mismatches found!")

# Token counts
total_gold = sum(len(t) for t in tokens)
total_produced = sum(len(d) for d in result)
print(f"\nTotal gold tokens: {total_gold}")
print(f"Total produced tokens: {total_produced}")
print(f"Match: {total_gold == total_produced}")

def run_single_seed(
    documents: List[Dict],
    seed: int,
    model_name: str = "bert-base-uncased",
    max_length: int = 128,
    device: str = None,
) -> Dict:
    """Run full pipeline for a single seed with diagnostics."""
    if device is None:
        device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

    # Split
    train_docs, test_docs = split_documents(documents, seed=seed)

    # Load model
    tokenizer, model, device = get_tokenizer_model(model_name, device)

    # Extract embeddings
    print(f"Extracting embeddings for {len(train_docs)} train + {len(test_docs)} test docs...")
    X_train, y_train, doc_ids_train = embed_documents(train_docs, tokenizer, model, device, max_length)
    X_test, y_test, doc_ids_test = embed_documents(test_docs, tokenizer, model, device, max_length)

    print(f"Train: {X_train.shape[0]} tokens, Test: {X_test.shape[0]} tokens")
    print(f"Test positive tokens: {y_test.sum()} / {len(y_test)} ({y_test.mean():.4f})")

    # Diagnostics: token norms
    train_norms = np.linalg.norm(X_train, axis=1)
    test_norms = np.linalg.norm(X_test, axis=1)
    print(f"Token norm mean: train={train_norms.mean():.4f}, test={test_norms.mean():.4f}")
    print(f"Token norm std: train={train_norms.std():.4f}, test={test_norms.std():.4f}")

    # Fit detector (authors' TokenCore)
    detector = create_detector()
    fit_detector(detector, X_train)
    token_scores = score_tokens(detector, X_test)

    # Compare with manual Euclidean nearest neighbor (should match authors' TokenCore)
    from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors as SKLearnNN
    manual_nbrs = SKLearnNN(n_neighbors=1).fit(X_train)
    manual_distances, _ = manual_nbrs.kneighbors(X_test)
    manual_scores = manual_distances.flatten()
    score_diff = np.abs(token_scores - manual_scores).max()
    print(f"Max score diff (authors vs manual sklearn NN): {score_diff:.6f}")

    # L2-normalized embeddings diagnostic
    from sklearn.preprocessing import normalize
    X_train_norm = normalize(X_train, norm='l2')
    X_test_norm = normalize(X_test, norm='l2')
    detector_norm = create_detector()
    fit_detector(detector_norm, X_train_norm)
    token_scores_norm = score_tokens(detector_norm, X_test_norm)
    token_auroc_norm = compute_metrics(y_test, token_scores_norm)['auroc']
    print(f"Token AUROC (L2-normalized embeddings): {token_auroc_norm:.4f}")

    # Token-level metrics (pooled micro)
    token_metrics = compute_metrics(y_test, token_scores)

    # Per-document-averaged token AUROC
    doc_token_aurocs = []
    for doc_id in np.unique(doc_ids_test):
        mask = doc_ids_test == doc_id
        y_doc = y_test[mask]
        s_doc = token_scores[mask]
        if len(np.unique(y_doc)) >= 2:
            doc_token_aurocs.append(compute_metrics(y_doc, s_doc)['auroc'])
    token_auroc_per_doc = float(np.mean(doc_token_aurocs)) if doc_token_aurocs else 0.5
    print(f"Token AUROC (per-document average, {len(doc_token_aurocs)} docs): {token_auroc_per_doc:.4f}")

    # Document-level metrics
    doc_labels = {d['id']: d['doc_label'] for d in documents}
    doc_scores, doc_true = compute_document_scores(token_scores, doc_ids_test, doc_labels)
    doc_metrics = compute_metrics(doc_true, doc_scores)

    # Sanity: training tokens should have low scores (near neighbors)
    train_scores = score_tokens(detector, X_train)
    print(f"Train token scores - mean: {train_scores.mean():.4f}, std: {train_scores.std():.4f}")
    print(f"Test token scores - mean: {token_scores.mean():.4f}, std: {token_scores.std():.4f}")

    return {
        'seed': seed,
        'token_auroc': token_metrics['auroc'],
        'token_auprc': token_metrics['auprc'],
        'token_auroc_per_doc': token_auroc_per_doc,
        'token_auroc_l2norm': token_auroc_norm,
        'doc_auroc': doc_metrics['auroc'],
        'doc_auprc': doc_metrics['auprc'],
        'n_train_docs': len(train_docs),
        'n_test_docs': len(test_docs),
        'n_bank_tokens': int(X_train.shape[0]),
        'n_test_tokens': int(X_test.shape[0]),
        'n_positive_tokens': int(y_test.sum()),
        'token_positive_rate': float(y_test.mean()),
        'train_token_norm_mean': float(train_norms.mean()),
        'train_token_norm_std': float(train_norms.std()),
        'test_token_norm_mean': float(test_norms.mean()),
        'test_token_norm_std': float(test_norms.std()),
        'train_token_score_mean': float(train_scores.mean()),
        'test_token_score_mean': float(token_scores.mean()),
        'score_diff_authors_vs_manual': float(score_diff),
    }

"""
Reconstruction of eval.split_anomaly_data from the authors' demo.ipynb.
The original module is not released, but the paper specifies:
"We use 50% normal documents as training data, the rest of data are set as testing including both normal and anomaly."
"""
import numpy as np
from typing import List, Tuple


def split_anomaly_data(
    tokens: List[List[str]],
    sentence_labels: List[int],
    labels: List[List[int]],
    seed: int = 42,
) -> Tuple[List[List[str]], List[int], List[List[str]], List[int], List[List[int]], List[List[int]]]:
    """
    Split data into train/test with 50% normal documents for training.
    
    Args:
        tokens: list of token lists per document
        sentence_labels: list of document-level labels (0/1)
        labels: list of token-level label lists
        seed: random seed for reproducibility
    
    Returns:
        X_train: token lists for training documents
        y_train: document labels for training documents
        X_test: token lists for test documents
        y_test: document labels for test documents
        z_train: token-level labels for training documents
        z_test: token-level labels for test documents
    """
    tokens = list(tokens)
    sentence_labels = list(sentence_labels)
    labels = [list(l) for l in labels]
    
    # Separate normal and anomalous documents
    normal_indices = [i for i, label in enumerate(sentence_labels) if label == 0]
    anomaly_indices = [i for i, label in enumerate(sentence_labels) if label == 1]
    
    # Shuffle normal indices with seed
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    rng.shuffle(normal_indices)
    
    # Take 50% of normal docs for training
    n_train_normal = len(normal_indices) // 2
    train_normal_indices = normal_indices[:n_train_normal]
    test_normal_indices = normal_indices[n_train_normal:]
    
    # Test set: remaining normal + all anomalous
    test_indices = test_normal_indices + anomaly_indices
    
    # Build train/test splits
    X_train = [tokens[i] for i in train_normal_indices]
    y_train = [sentence_labels[i] for i in train_normal_indices]
    z_train = [labels[i] for i in train_normal_indices]
    
    X_test = [tokens[i] for i in test_indices]
    y_test = [sentence_labels[i] for i in test_indices]
    z_test = [labels[i] for i in test_indices]
    
    return X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test

"""
Reproduce TokenCore token-level AUROC on Grammar dataset (Claim C1).
Following the authors' demo.ipynb protocol exactly:
- Model: bert-base-cased
- Split: eval.split_anomaly_data (50% normal docs for training)
- Embeddings: align.extract_word_embeddings with max-pooling over subwords
- Detector: TokenCore (notebook uses TextCore, but repo has TokenCore)

import json
import os
import sys
import time
import numpy as np
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

# Add src to path
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'src'))

from data_grammar import load_grammar, verify_dataset
from embed_bert import get_tokenizer_model, embed_documents
from detector import create_detector, fit_detector, score_tokens
from evaluate import compute_metrics, compute_document_scores
from eval_module import split_anomaly_data


def run_single_seed(
    documents: List[Dict],

    max_length: int = 128,

        split_anomaly_data(tokens, sentence_labels, labels, seed=seed)

    print(f"Train docs anomalous: {sum(y_train_doc)}, Test docs anomalous: {sum(y_test_doc)}")

    # Load model

    test_data = embed_documents_from_tokens(X_test_tokens, z_test_tokens, tokenizer, model, device, max_length)

    X_train = np.array([item['embedding'] for sent in train_data for item in sent])
    z_train = [item['label'] for sent in train_data for item in sent]
    X_test = np.array([item['embedding'] for sent in test_data for item in sent])
    z_test = [item['label'] for sent in test_data for item in sent]

    print(f"Train: {X_train.shape[0]} tokens, Test: {X_test.shape[0]} tokens")
    print(f"Test positive tokens: {sum(z_test)} / {len(z_test)} ({sum(z_test)/len(z_test):.4f})")

    # Diagnostics: token norms
    train_norms = np.linalg.norm(X_train, axis=1)
    test_norms = np.linalg.norm(X_test, axis=1)
    print(f"Token norm mean: train={train_norms.mean():.4f}, test={test_norms.mean():.4f}")
    print(f"Token norm std: train={train_norms.std():.4f}, test={test_norms.std():.4f}")

    # Fit detector (authors' TokenCore)
    detector = create_detector()
    fit_detector(detector, X_train)
    token_scores = score_tokens(detector, X_test)

    doc_ids_test = np.array(doc_ids_test)

    doc_token_aurocs = []
